role.altitude: The planner keeps working with consultants, talking to groups, visiting sites and interviewing people; lookups, comment chains, counting and coding by hand shrink.
skills_to_grow: Keeping GIS queries, the codebook and the fact library current
role.ambitious_version: A planner who screens every parcel in the municipality for development, not only the sites colleagues suggest.

tasks.short: Write the brief for economic consultants or architects, send it, hold progress meetings, review drafts against the brief, send comments, keep the issue log and accept the final deliverable.

steps.what: Urban planner writes the brief for the economic consultant or architect with plan goals and constraints
Urban planner checks the final brief and base data: goals, constraints and requirements, and the consultant or architect they go to
Urban planner sends the brief and base data to the consultant or architect
Urban planner coordinates work with the consultants or architects in progress meetings and design workshops
Urban planner reviews draft studies and designs against the brief and the plan constraints

loop.input: The brief's numbered requirements and the consultant's draft.
loop.output: Per requirement: the passage and page in the draft that addresses it, or 'not found'.
loop.check: Every 'found' must quote a passage that exists on the cited page; the planner reads each cited passage, judges whether it meets the requirement, and reads every 'not found' before writing comments.
loop.why_not_simpler: Drafts do not follow the brief's numbering, so a requirement can be met anywhere in the text.

steps.what: Urban planner writes review comments on the draft in the issue register
Urban planner checks the final comments: each against the review findings and the brief, and the consultant they go to
Urban planner releases the checked comments to the consultant: by e-mail today, in the shared issue register after the change
Urban planner keeps a log of agreements, open issues and decisions across meetings and comment rounds
Urban planner checks the final deliverable against the brief and the issue log
Urban planner accepts the checked deliverable and tells the consultant

approvals.approved_version: The brief with its numbered requirements and the base data exactly as checked by the planner in s2a, sent once to the contracted consultant or architect; any change needs a new check.
The review comments on this draft exactly as checked by the planner in s5b, released once to the consultant in the shared issue register; any change needs a new check.
Acceptance of the final deliverable version exactly as checked by the planner in s7, sent once to the consultant; any later change to the deliverable needs a new check.

tasks.design: A brief template pulls goals and the constraint list from the plan file so the planner writes only what is new. For each draft, a bounded step maps the brief's numbered requirements to the passages that meet them, with quotes the planner reads, and comments and agreements go into one issue register in the {PROJECT} tool instead of mail threads. Meetings, design talks, comments and acceptance stay with the planner.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements were checked by rereading the whole draft, and agreements were spread over e-mails and meeting notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Project tools keep issue registers shared with outside parties; language models can map requirements to passages with quotes.
tasks.still_hard: Steering a consultant or architect toward a better design is a conversation.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing where an architect's design fights the plan and finding the compromise.
tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time chasing what was agreed; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Whether one issue register with the consultant cuts comment rounds.

evidence.claim: Language models can match listed requirements to passages in a long document and quote them for checking.
Project tools can share an issue register with outside parties.

assumptions: Boundary: from the brief to the accepted deliverable; hiring the consultant and the consultant's own study work are outside.
Input contract for s4: briefs with numbered requirements, written in the template by the planner; drafts delivered as text documents by the consultant; fallback is reading in full.
The consultant uses the shared issue register; if not, the planner copies comments into it.

Meetings and acceptance do not change. Writing review comments is a first write and keeps its full time; s6 keeps 60 because meeting agreements are still written, while copying comments into the log goes.
unknowns: How many consultant assignments run at the same time.
Whether consultants accept a shared register.
research_questions: How many comment rounds per deliverable before and after the register?
How often does the mapping miss a requirement that was met?

already_counted.description: Urban planner reads mapped passages and every 'not found' requirement.

incremental.description: Urban planner keeps the brief template and requirement numbering current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one architect on a small design who does not use the shared register (s6 keeps 90), with few requirements to map (s4 keeps 95) and a brief written mostly new (s1 keeps 95) (1.9); high: several consultants on a large plan with many draft rounds (10.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather sustainability facts, prepare presentations and fact sheets, advocate at meetings with groups and agencies, answer questions and follow up on commitments.

steps.what: Urban planner gathers sustainability facts and figures (energy, green space, heat, water) from monitors and reports
Urban planner prepares presentations and fact sheets for the audience

loop.input: The figures from the sustainability dashboard, the approved policy texts and the planner's points for this audience.
loop.output: Draft fact sheet text and slide text in plain language.
loop.check: Every figure must match the dashboard dataset and every policy statement must quote an approved policy paragraph, or it is marked; the planner reads each statement against its figure or paragraph and edits all text before use.
loop.stop: One draft per audience and version of points; if rejected, the planner writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each audience needs its own wording; a template gives the layout, not the explanation.

steps.what: Urban planner advocates sustainability at meetings with community groups, agencies, the public and interest groups
Urban planner answers questions from residents and groups: by phone, and by e-mail starting from drafted replies

loop.input: The question and the library of approved answers and policy texts.
loop.output: A draft reply citing the answer entries or policy paragraphs it uses.
loop.check: Every statement must cite an entry in the library, or the reply is marked; replies to questions with no matching entry are not drafted; the planner reads each drafted reply against the question and the cited entry and edits it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Questions are free text; a list of answers still has to be matched and worded for the person.

steps.what: Urban planner checks each final e-mail reply: that it answers the question, matches the cited library entry, and goes to the right resident or group
Urban planner sends the checked reply
Urban planner logs contacts and commitments with groups and follows up

approvals.approved_version: The e-mail reply exactly as checked by the planner in s4b, sent once to the resident or group who asked; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: A sustainability dashboard in {BI} shows the current figures, so the planner stops collecting them per talk. A bounded step drafts fact sheet and slide text per audience, with every figure checked against the dashboard and every policy line against approved texts, and drafts replies to questions from an approved answer library; the planner edits, checks and sends each e-mail reply. Meetings and follow-up stay with the planner, who writes contacts and commitments in a stakeholder log in the {CRM} instead of a spreadsheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures were gathered from several reports for each talk, and the same questions were answered from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Monitors publish figures as datasets; language models draft plain text that can be checked against approved sources.
tasks.human_edge: Being trusted in a room of sceptical residents.

ambition.what: Fact sheets in plain language for neighbourhoods that are not reached today.

tasks.altitude: More of the planner's time goes to meetings and less to preparing them; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Which figures residents ask about most.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft plain-language text whose figures and statements can be checked against a dataset and approved texts.
Text made with AI to inform the public must be disclosed unless a person edits it under responsibility.

assumptions: Boundary: from gathering figures to follow-up with groups; campaigns run by the communications team are outside.
Input contract for s1: the sustainability monitor published as a dataset by the policy team; fallback is the reports.
Input contract for s4: an answer library of approved texts kept by the planner and the communications adviser.
The planner edits all drafted text, so it is published under the municipality's responsibility.
Meetings do not change. The stakeholder log is a first record of contacts and commitments, so s5 keeps its full time.
unknowns: How many advocacy meetings per month.
Whether a sustainability monitor exists as data.
research_questions: How much drafted text survives the planner's edit?
Which questions have no answer in the library?

already_counted.description: Urban planner edits drafted fact sheets and slides.

incremental.description: Urban planner keeps the answer library current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a few large meetings with one fixed presentation, so drafting per audience saves little (s2 keeps 90), and few questions match the library (s4 keeps 90) (8.3); high: many small groups with their own material and questions (14.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: List candidate sites, check ownership and rights in the land registry, check zoning and environmental constraints, visit sites, contact owners and write the availability overview.

steps.what: Urban planner lists candidate sites for development from municipal land and GIS maps
Urban planner investigates property availability: owner, rights and encumbrances per parcel in the land registry
Urban planner checks zoning, soil and environmental constraints per site
Urban planner visits the most promising sites
Urban planner contacts owners or their agents about willingness to sell or develop
Urban planner writes the site availability overview with findings per site

tasks.design: A saved GIS query ({OTHER}) lists parcels that meet the site requirements (size, use, location), and a batch request through the municipality's land registry connection ({GOV_PORTAL}) returns owner, rights and encumbrances per parcel into one table. Zoning, soil and environmental layers are overlaid per site, and an overview generator fills the site table from these records; the planner adds observations from visits and owners' positions from calls and writes the findings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each parcel was looked up one by one in the registry and the plan viewer.
tasks.enabler_now: Land registry connections return extracts in batch; GIS overlays of rule and constraint layers are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Owner willingness and site quality only show on site and on the phone.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a site that no query would find and getting an owner to talk.

ambition.what: Screen every parcel in the municipality when a development need comes up, not only known sites.

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time on lookups and more on visits and owners; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Which registry rights block deals most often.

evidence.claim: Land registries offer extracts per parcel through system connections, including owner and recorded rights.
Owner details of private persons are personal data and may be used only for the development purpose.

assumptions: Boundary: from site requirements to the availability overview; negotiations and purchase are outside.

Input contract for s2: parcel ids from the s1 query; extracts from the land registry connection the municipality already has; about 80% of parcels resolve without reading deeds; fallback is the registry website per parcel.
Registry fees per extract are a running cost, not labour.
Visits and owner calls do not change; owner positions in the overview come from the actual calls.
unknowns: How many site searches per year and parcels per search.
Whether the municipality has a registry connection for batch extracts.
research_questions: How many good sites did the query find that colleagues did not suggest?
How often do recorded rights change a site's ranking?

already_counted.description: Urban planner checks query results and reads deeds for parcels that do not resolve.
Urban planner checks overlay results per site.

incremental.description: Urban planner keeps GIS queries and layers current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a search across a few known sites with complex ownership, so many deeds are read (s2 keeps 70) and the query adds little (s1 keeps 80) (24.7); high: a municipality-wide search over many simple parcels (39.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design the survey and interview guide, collect answers, analyse results, interview people, write notes, inspect sites and count traffic, record findings and summarise the factors affecting land use.

steps.what: Urban planner designs the survey questionnaire and interview guide on zoning, traffic and housing factors
Residents and businesses answer the survey
Urban planner analyses survey results and codes the open answers

loop.input: Each open answer and the survey's fixed codebook.
loop.output: One or more codes per answer.
loop.check: The planner double-codes a random sample of at least 50 answers and reads answers the step marks unclear; if agreement is below the agreed rate the codes are not used and the planner codes by hand; closed questions are counted by plain code.
loop.stop: One coding pass per codebook version.
loop.why_not_simpler: Open answers state the same issue in many words; keyword rules miss most.

steps.what: Urban planner asks each interviewee for agreement to record and notes the answer
Urban planner conducts interviews with residents, businesses and stakeholders
Urban planner writes up interview notes

loop.input: The transcript of the recorded interview and the interview guide.
loop.output: Draft notes per guide question with the interviewee's points.
loop.check: Every point must cite a transcript time, or it is dropped; the planner listens to cited passages where unsure and corrects the notes; recordings are deleted after the notes are final.
loop.why_not_simpler: Answers wander between questions; a transcript alone is too long to use.

steps.what: Urban planner conducts site inspections: observes land use, buildings and street conditions and takes photos
Urban planner counts traffic flow at key points on site
Urban planner records inspection findings in a spreadsheet back at the office
Urban planner summarises the factors that affect land usage from surveys, interviews and inspections

tasks.design: Questions come from a question bank in the survey tool ({OTHER}); closed answers are counted by plain code and a bounded step codes open answers to a fixed codebook, released only if the planner's sample double-coding agrees. Recorded interviews are transcribed and drafted into notes per guide question with time references for the planner to correct. Site inspections stay on foot, but findings go straight into a field form on a tablet, and where roads have counting loops, counts come from the national traffic data portal instead of counting by hand.
tasks.previous_blocker: Open answers were coded by hand, notes were typed from memory, and inspections were written up twice.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models code open answers close to a second human coder; speech-to-text and field forms are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Getting people to talk honestly and seeing what a street is like at different times.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what residents worry about that no question asked.
tasks.altitude: The planner spends the time on more interviews or sites; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Which agreement rate makes coded answers safe to use.

evidence.claim: On 'most important issue' answers with 50 codes, the best language model coded 93.9% correctly against 94.7% for a second human coder.
A national road traffic data portal publishes traffic data from road counting points.
Recording interviews needs the interviewee's agreement, and notes with personal data follow the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the research question to the summary of land use factors; the plan itself is outside.

Input contract for s7: counts from the national traffic data portal for locations with counting loops; about half of the planner's count points have one; the rest are counted by hand, so s7 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s8: a field form on a tablet with location, photo and observation fields; records are the actual observations made on site.
Residents answer online as they do today; their time is shown in s2 and is outside the planner's savings.
Interviews and site visits do not change. Recording agreement is asked and noted before each interview (s4a); without it, notes are written as today.
unknowns: How many surveys and interviews per study.
Which count points have counting loops.
research_questions: What agreement rate do coded open answers reach on this codebook?
How much time do field forms save on writing up inspections?

already_counted.description: Urban planner double-codes a sample of open answers and checks the counts.
Urban planner corrects drafted interview notes.

incremental.description: Urban planner keeps the codebook and question bank current.
Urban planner deletes recordings after the notes are final.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small study with few open answers (s3 keeps 80) and unrecorded interviews (s5 keeps 100) (11.4); high: a large resident survey with recorded interviews (22.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
